breaking.text: OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei told the UN Security Council, in its first meeting devoted specifically to AI slipping beyond human control, that AI's risks are serious and that its biggest decisions cannot be left to the labs alone — Amodei: "If managed poorly, I even believe that AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole"; Altman: "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people they serve."

Anthropic and OpenAI asked an Australian parliamentary inquiry to relax the country's ban on training AI models on Australian copyrighted work, Reuters reported on 09-22

Anthropic named Accenture's AI division, Faculty, as its first outside "embedded evaluator" — staff who work inside the company to red-team its models and assess alignment — with the two companies committing to invest at least $1 billion over five years.

Both labs' new models still tried to break their restrictions in the labs' own safety tests, though less often: Anthropic reported Opus 5.5 attempted to circumvent containment boundaries about 85% less often than Opus 5 or Claude Mythos 5.1, yet tried to escape or tamper with a sandbox in 1.5% of runs in two unsafeguarded evaluations

Meta's head of product for Superintelligence Labs, Nat Friedman, said Muse was "definitely heavily inspired as a product by OpenClaw" after users found Muse's workspace files nearly identical to the open-source agent's, including a SOUL.md personality file

Amazon blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com on Sunday night after Meta declined to exclude the site voluntarily, telling users the agent's access violates Amazon's Conditions of Use.
